Ultra HD 4K 120fps cinematic video, 2.39:1 widescreen aspect ratio, HDR Dolby Vision, extreme dynamic range, exclusive Cyberpunk neon color grading, combining silky high-speed slow motion with sharp quick cuts.
A cool and sassy young Caucasian woman with waist-length ice-blue hair blown violently backward by the high-speed airflow, every strand of hair distinct and fluttering fiercely in the wind, with pink and blue neon reflections on the ends. She wears a shiny black cropped leather jacket over a black crop top, a black mini skirt paired with black high-top motorcycle boots, and a black choker around her neck that sways with her body movements. The smooth and glossy surface of the leather jacket constantly reflects the flowing neon lights around, and the hem of the jacket flips up violently in the wind. She leans her body forward significantly to lower her center of gravity, grips the handlebars tightly with both hands, stares ahead with sharp and focused eyes, naturally leans inward when cornering, and the muscle lines of her legs are tense.
She is driving a fully glossy black futuristic heavy Cyberpunk motorcycle. The front and rear wheels of the motorcycle emit dazzling ice-blue annular cold light, forming continuous blue light trail streaks when rotating at high speed. The headlights shoot out two sharp cold white light beams, cutting through the night and illuminating the road ahead. The metal surface of the motorcycle body reflects the flowing neon lights of the city, the engine vibrates slightly, the exhaust pipe intermittently sprays light blue plasma tail flames, and the holographic dashboard on the handlebars flashes with beating blue numbers and lines. The motorcycle gallops on the urban elevated road at a speed of 120km/h, and the tires roll over the wet asphalt road, splashing tiny crystal water droplets.
Opening low-angle upward tracking shot, starting from a close-up of the motorcycle's front wheel, following the vehicle as it accelerates sharply with a slight vibration close to the ground

inputs.text: A medium close-up shot features a Caucasian man with a closely shaven head and face, wearing a black baseball cap with "PNTR" in white letters on the front, and a dark grey t-shirt with "JUST DO IT" visible across his chest. A small black microphone is clipped to his shirt collar. He is positioned slightly to the left of the frame, looking intently downwards and to his right, his eyes focused off-camera. His facial expression is one of deep concentration, with his brow slightly furrowed. As he looks down, a quick sniff sound is heard, and then he speaks with a deep male voice and a slightly frustrated tone, saying, "I think it's so bad." The camera remains static throughout, maintaining a shallow depth of field, which keeps the man in sharp focus while the background is softly blurred, revealing a light-colored wall with white wooden shelving or trim, and a partially open white wooden door on the right. After a brief pause, another short, audible sniff is heard. The man then continues to speak, his voice maintaining the same quality, as he states, "So bad. So bad." He elaborates further, emphasizing his point with a final statement, "This got to be, it's got to be the worst tool I've ever seen."
